Definition: El-Bethel, the title given to a consecrated spot by Jacob
BiblicalUsage: El-Bethel is the title Jacob gave to a consecrated spot. In Genesis 35:7, Jacob builds an altar at Bethel and calls the place El-beth-el, 'God of Bethel', because God appeared to him there as he fled from his brother. It is a compound name, built from the word for God joined to Bethel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe El-Bethel matters because the names we give to places where God meets us keep the memory of what He did. That is why Jacob's name for the spot still stands.
